title: LatticeNav: Progressive Sidebar Compression with Route Intent Signals
creator: Ana Rodriguez
description:
Summary: Design an adaptive sidebar and routing model—LatticeNav—that compresses into a progressive micro-rail while surfacing route intent signals (rollout status, cost hotspots, active workspace indicators). This ticket captures the prototype, interaction patterns, and acceptance criteria for the Console information architecture change affecting workspace switching, per-route dashboards, and rollout access flows.

Goals: 
- Make workspace switching feel continuous: preserve scroll/selection context across switches and show lightweight previews of last-used dashboard.
- Reduce cognitive load in the primary rail by collapsing low-frequency items into a micro-rail while keeping key SLO/rollout signals visible at a glance.
- Expose cost and rollout state as low-fidelity badges and progressive overlays rather than deep drill-downs.
- Ensure keyboard-first navigation and screen-reader semantics for compressed states.

Scope (this ticket): 
- Interaction spec and Figma prototype for three states: Expanded, Collapsed (icon-focused), and Micro-rail (hover/peek).
- Route intent signals: rollout state (canary/stable/fallback), cost heat (low/medium/high) mapped to badge color and subtle motion.
- Workspace switcher transition patterns (crossfade + retained selection history).
- Acceptance criteria and usability test plan for internal PM and Eng review.

Out of scope: A/B rollout plumbing on backend, RBAC surface design, or long-form billing pages (these are follow-ups).

Design details: 
- IA: primary sections become: Home / Models / Deployments / Observability / Billing / Settings. Secondary items (Integrations, Marketplace, Admin consoles) are collapsed into a secondary group accessible from the micro-rail.
- Intent signals: small triangular chevron on the rail item indicates an active rollout; a thin vertical bar (cost heat) scaled by recent tokens spends; tooltip reveals short context (last 24h cost delta, rollout progress e.g., 12% canary).
- Compression rules: items with <2 weekly clicks eligible for auto-compress; user can pin to force-expanded. Compression is per-workspace and persisted to user preferences.
- Workspace continuity: switching preserves the previously open route state (if returning within 10 minutes) and shows a top-of-panel micro-preview with last error/warning counts and active canaries.
- Accessibility: ARIA labels for compressed icons, focus traps for micro-rail, sufficient color contrast for badges, motion reduced setting respected.

Metrics & success criteria: 
- Reduce average nav time to dashboard by 15% for power users (1W pilot).
- 90% of participants in internal usability test can locate rollout state within 3 interactions.
- No regression in keyboard nav coverage; automated e2e test cases pass.

Deliverables: 
- Figma prototype with three interaction states (link below).
- PRD section for Console IA Refresh describing routing semantics and persistence.
- Usability test plan and session notes.
- Handoff tokens and component specs for Engineering.

Risks & trade-offs: 
- Over-compression could hide seldom-used but important admin surfaces; mitigation: pin/unpin affordance and a discoverability hint on first use.
- Cost heat approximation may confuse users if sampling window differs from billing; mitigation: tooltip clarifies sampling window and links to billing page.

Next steps: 
- Complete prototype iteration based on Eng feasibility meeting (scheduled 2026-03-16).
- Run 6 internal usability sessions (Design + SEs) by 2026-03-19.
- Prepare a staged rollout plan with console product and SEs once engineering estimates are finalized.
